extracted.intended_audience: museum professionals, grant program staff, and program evaluators (museums applying for or managing MFA grants)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and metrics used to describe, categorize, and evaluate museum projects funded by the Museums for America (MFA) program, including primary activity areas, associated activities, outputs, partnerships, audience outcomes, and implementation characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary activity area (project focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify the grant-funded project by its primary focus: Programming, Exhibitions, Technology/Online Resources, Digitization/Collections, or Organizational Development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to report the portion of MFA funding devoted to each area (e.g., % of respondents indicating greatest amount devoted to Exhibitions, Technology, etc.). Also used to analyze cross-over with other activity areas (percent of projects with primary focus X that also conducted activities in Y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming activities (content and delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programming activities include developing on-site educational programs, interpretive programs or materials, demonstrations/workshops, lectures, curriculum guides, in-school programs, training sessions, community discussion groups, afterschool programs, classes, internships/apprenticeships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and measures include percent of projects conducting education programs or interpretive programs; typical accompanying activities (hiring contractors, training, research/evaluation, creating interpreter programs); use of programming as a secondary activity in exhibitions or technology projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibitions activities (design, fabrication, upgrade)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibition-related tasks such as planning a new exhibit; developing exhibit concepts; fabricating new exhibits; researching new exhibits; upgrading or expanding current exhibits; creating traveling exhibits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported prevalence (e.g., % that developed a new exhibit, % that upgraded current exhibits). Guidance notes include adapting exhibits to integrate hands-on activities and expanding accessibility for students with special needs; exhibitions often accompanied by programming and organizational development tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology / online resources activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology activities include updating/creating websites, creating online exhibitions, developing media-based products, developing high-tech interactive exhibitions, creating audio tours, purchasing/upgrading hardware and software, and managing collections databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported metrics: percent of projects conducting web updates, hardware purchases, collections accessibility work; technology projects commonly cross over with digitization, organizational development, programming, and exhibitions; examples include creating distance learning modules and web-accessible archives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digitization and collections activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities such as creating new digital content, converting non-digital content to digital, repurposing digital content, digitizing collections, conducting inventories/cataloging, implementing collections management systems, creating public collection guides, and creating new collection management procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures include percent of projects that digitized collections, proportion of collections digitized (e.g., % projects that digitized more than half their collections), and related technology/development activities. Guidance highlights digitization's role in preservation and increased access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational development activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization-level activities related to management, training, and resource development: providing staff/volunteer/docent training, supporting research/evaluation programs, developing management plans, hiring consultants, contracting services, hiring part-/full-time staff, and creating/expanding interpreter or volunteer programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported prevalence (e.g., % that conducted training or hired new staff). Examples include creating new positions (Training and Development Manager), instituting staff training modules and rewards programs, and embedding visitor service standards into performance evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity overlap / cross-cutting activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure and characterization of how projects combine multiple activity types (e.g., Technology-focused projects also including digitization, organizational development, programming, exhibitions, or collections activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as percentages of primary-focus projects that also conducted other activities (e.g., 71% of Technology-focused projects also entailed digitization). Use to understand multi-component projects and resource distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum size and grant award association
rubrics_metrics.description: Association between project types and museum size (small, medium, large) and award size (small < $50,000; medium $50,000–$99,999; large ≥ $100,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to report distributions (e.g., large/medium museums conducted the greatest portion of Programming projects; Technology projects more frequently by large institutions; percent of projects by award size). Helps interpret capacity and scale effects on project type and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships (presence, number, and partner types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent and type of partnerships used to implement projects: whether projects involved partners, number of partners (1–2, 3–4, 5+), and categories of partner organizations (community organizations, educational institutions, government organizations, museums and libraries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnerships defined as outside organizations providing cash or in-kind resources. Metrics reported include percent of projects with partners and the mix of partner types (e.g., arts and culture groups, local businesses, schools). Notes that smaller museums were more likely to engage partners; grant size had limited effect on partnership patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and professional development outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation and delivery of training and professional development for staff, volunteers, and docents, including development of curricula, new training positions, and institutionalization of training programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include developing visitor service training modules, creating new managerial positions, integrating training into onboarding, and linking training outcomes to performance standards. Reported as common organizational development activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation and assessment (research, measurement tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation of research and evaluation activities, including visitor experience research, project evaluation, development and use of assessment tools, and outcomes-based planning tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: use of MFA’s outcomes-based planning tools, hiring consultants to develop social network maps to measure long-term impacts, creating assessment tools to evaluate exhibit effectiveness, and collecting evaluation data (surveys, usage metrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience and community engagement metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative and qualitative measures of community engagement and audience outcomes, such as attendance numbers, service counts (health screenings, signups), website visits, newsletter subscribers, community contributions (user comments, donations), and changes in staff language capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Corona Plaza festivals with 2,500 attendees each, 1,500 health screenings, 900 insurance signups; JoCoHistory.net reporting nearly one million monthly views and newsletter growth from 800 to 6,000 readers. Guidance suggests using these metrics to evaluate reach and community impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts to increase accessibility and inclusion in exhibits and programs, such as expanding accessibility for students with special needs, multilingual programming, hiring bilingual staff, and making exhibits more accessible to diverse audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include upgrading exhibits for accessibility, offering programs in multiple languages, and increasing Spanish-speaking staff from ~3% to >20%. Accessibility frequently appears as an explicit goal in exhibitions and organizational development projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability and follow-on funding
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which MFA-funded projects leverage additional funding or lead to sustained programs or new initiatives beyond the grant period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: MFA-funded Corona Plaza leading to new funding for Corona Studios; JoCoHistory.net sustained by county agency support. Guidance: report whether projects continued, secured additional support, or institutionalized activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational alignment and curricular relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Alignment of programs and digital/education offerings with formal education standards (e.g., state curriculum standards) and targeted grade levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include distance learning modules aligned to Virginia learning standards for third grade and curricular modules for grades 4–12 using historic photographs. Use alignment as a measure of program relevance to schools and educators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technology to increase public access
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and implementation of online tools and web resources to broaden access to collections and programs: searchable online databases, web-accessible archives, online curriculum guides, user contribution/comment features, and integration of multimedia for public engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured by counts such as % of projects creating online access, website traffic, and user contributions. Examples: JoCoHistory.net enabling public comments that led to new donated materials and expansion of holdings.
